model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: AFFO per share, organic. Aggregate AFFO grew 13.7% a year FY2022-FY2025 (805.8 -> 1,183.6) but almost all of it was the all-stock Physicians Realty merger (shares 547m -> 696m); AFFO per share went from ~1.47 to ~1.69, 4.7% a year, and falls ~5% in FY2026E.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (4.3% / 2.2%) diverges more than 30% from revenue CAGR (11.0% / 11.4%), and both are merger-distorted: the March 2024 Physicians Realty merger added ~150m shares. Per-share figures are the meaningful ones. EPS CAGRs are omitted: GAAP EPS (0.92 FY2022 -> 0.10 FY2025) is driven by depreciation, impairments and disposal gains.
historical_growth.notes: fcf series is AFFO (KPI table, available FY2021-FY2025 only, so no 5-year figure; the 4-year FY2021-FY2025 CAGR is 12.9%). SBC is ~1.2% of AFFO and flat (14.5, 15.5, 14.4, ~17.7 in FY2026E), so the SBC-adjusted and reported series grow at the same rate.

scenario_narratives.base: AFFO per share bottoms in FY2026-27 at about 1.60 and then grows 3-3.5% organically as lab leases signed in late 2026 commence and outpatient escalators run, capitalised at a 9.25% cost of equity. The dividend of 1.22 stays covered at roughly 76%.
scenario_narratives.bull: A real lab recovery: occupancy back above 93% by 2029, senior housing same-store NOI still growing in the teens through 2027, AFFO per share growing 4-6% for five years, and an 8.5% cost of equity as the lab discount closes.
scenario_narratives.bear: The lab downturn is structural rather than cyclical: NIH and biotech funding stay weak, new supply keeps clearing, AFFO per share falls about 9% over two years, and the equity is priced at 10.25% for the refinancing and re-leasing risk.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Healthpeak is valued as a stream of AFFO attributable to common holders, after stock compensation, capitalised at the cost of equity with no further deduction for debt. Only organic growth is credited, since the whole of AFFO is treated as distributed. The current price implies roughly an 8% AFFO yield and a 6% dividend yield on trough earnings; the value turns on whether lab occupancy at 85.9% is a trough or a way-point.
key_risks_to_valuation: Lab segment (about 28% of revenue, concentrated in South San Francisco, Boston and San Diego): each further point of occupancy lost, or a downward rent re-mark on renewal, comes straight out of AFFO
AFFO capex covers recurring spend only; first-generation TI and redevelopment needed to re-lease lab space sit outside AFFO and could make it overstate distributable cash
Refinancing: 9.4bn of debt, with 2027 term-loan and note maturities resetting while the 10-year Treasury is above 5%
Janus Living: a 69%-owned, separately listed subsidiary whose equity raises dilute Healthpeak's share of the fastest-growing segment, and whose share price has run far above its IPO price
Rate sensitivity: one point on the cost of equity moves the base value by roughly 15%
Policy: Medicaid and ACA subsidy changes on tenant and operator credit; NIH funding on lab demand

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 15.70-22.95
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL via DOC.duckdb / DOC_Metrics.csv; AFFO, FFO as Adjusted, share counts, debt and dividends from DOC_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt (10-Q, balance sheet 2026-09-30) and DOC_Annual_FY2025.txt
data_sources.qualitative: DOC_Analysis.json (2026-11-15); FY2026 guidance as raised with Q3-2026 results on 2026-11-02 (FFO as Adjusted 1.76-1.78 a share, same-store cash NOI +0.5% to +2.0%)

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K AFFO reconciliation, 'Stock-based compensation amortization expense' 14,410 (DOC_Annual_FY2025.txt:7584); 9M-2026 13,265 (Q3-2026 10-Q). This is the amount AFFO adds back, so it is the amount the house basis takes out again. The cash-flow-statement figure in core_metrics (20.0) includes amounts capitalised or classified in transaction costs.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-13T21:00:02Z regular close (Friday; valuation run on the weekend)
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted FFO/AFFO share base at 30 Sep 2026: 690m common (10-Q) + ~6m Healthpeak OP units + ~13m shares issuable on DownREIT units + ~1m RSUs = ~709.5m. Cross-check: 9M-2026 diluted FFO as Adjusted 951.5 / 709.5 = 1.34 a share, and FY guidance 1.76-1.78 implies a Q4 of ~0.43, in line with Q3's 309.2 / 709.5. Because the unit holders are in the denominator, their distributions (~18m a year) are added back to the numerator. Held flat: SBC is expensed in the flows and buybacks (101.7m in 9M-2026) are not capitalised.
inputs.wacc_rationale: The 'wacc' field is a COST OF EQUITY, because AFFO is a post-interest flow. USD build: 10-year Treasury 5.15% (Yahoo ^TNX, 2026-11-13) + beta ~0.9 x 4.5% ERP = ~9.2%, rounded to 9.25% base. Bull 8.5% (lab risk recedes, rates ease), bear 10.25% (lab downturn persists and 2027 refinancing lands at wider spreads). Net debt is held at zero so the 9.4bn of debt is not deducted a second time.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: ground-lease cost is already inside AFFO.
inputs.nci_treatment: AFFO is 'applicable to common shares': the ~31% of Janus Living owned by outside holders, the Brookfield JV's 49% and other partners' shares of FFO, AFFO capex and entrance fees are already netted in the reconciliation. No separate NCI deduction, and no separate add for the Janus Living stake, whose earnings are already in the flow.
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT AFFO capitalisation at the cost of equity, run through the Drivers engine with net debt at zero. Chosen per the dcf-methods routing table (REIT / property trust row): AFFO is after interest, so FCF/WACC less net debt would count the debt twice, and GAAP net income is dominated by depreciation, impairments and change-of-control gains (FY2025 EPS 0.10, 9M-2026 0.38 including a 138m gain). First valuation of this ticker; no prior model. ENGINE MAPPING: 'ebitda_margin_path' is diluted AFFO as the company defines it divided by consolidated revenue; 'sbc_pct_path' is stock-compensation amortisation, so the house value is AFFO less SBC and the street value is company AFFO; D&A, capex, tax and working capital are zero because AFFO is already after recurring capex, straight-line rent and cash tax. 'growth_rates' year 1 is consolidated revenue growth for FY2026E (9M actual 2,345.4 + Q4 ~835 = ~3,180, +12.7%, inflated by Janus Living acquisitions that are ~31% owned by outsiders); the year-1 margin of 35.63% is set so year-1 AFFO equals the FY2026 estimate. From year 2 the margin is flat, so the growth path IS the AFFO growth path. FY2026E AFFO: 9M actual 850.1 (rebuilt from the Q3 10-Q reconciliation: FFO as Adjusted 938.3 + deferred financing 25.9 + entrance fees 37.3 + SBC 13.3 + deferred tax 4.0 - AFFO capex 103.7 - straight-line 36.0 - market-lease 19.5 - other 9.6; the same build reproduces the 9M-2025 KPI of 904.0 exactly) + Q4 ~265 (Q3 was 274.6; Q4 capex is seasonally heavier) = ~1,115, plus ~18 of unit distributions = ~1,133 diluted, or ~1.60 a share against a 1.22 dividend (76% payout). That is down ~5% on FY2025's 1.69: lab occupancy 97.9% -> 85.9% in six quarters, AFFO capex up 36%, and Janus Living dilution. TIMING: fy0 is FY2025, so FY2026 is discounted as a full year although the valuation date is mid-November; the missing ~10 months of accretion and the ~10 months of FY2026 AFFO already paid out roughly cancel (about +2% on the base value, not applied). GROWTH IS ORGANIC ONLY: capitalising the whole of AFFO treats it as distributed, so growth funded by the retained 24% or by new equity is deliberately excluded. Note AFFO capex is recurring capex only; first-generation TI, redevelopment and development spend (material in lab) sit outside it, which is one reason the cost of equity is not set lower. CROSS-CHECK, not in the value: Healthpeak holds 138.8m Janus Living shares plus OP units; at JAN's 2026-11-13 close that stake is worth roughly 4.4bn, about 6 a DOC share, against an IPO price of 20.00 in March 2026. A market that values DOC at ~12.5x AFFO while valuing its senior-housing subsidiary this richly is implicitly pricing the outpatient and lab remainder very low.

bear.narrative: Lab occupancy slides to the low 80s and renewals re-mark down in South San Francisco and Boston, re-leasing capex stays elevated, and 2027-28 maturities refinance 150bp+ above coupon. AFFO per share falls to ~1.45 by 2028 and only then grows at 2%.

base.narrative: FY2026E AFFO ~1.60 a share. 2027 +1.5%: lab occupancy troughs but the 2026 average was above the exit rate, and 2027 term-loan and note maturities refinance above their coupons; outpatient escalators and senior housing offset. 3-3.5% thereafter as signed lab leases commence, fading to 2.5%.

bull.narrative: Lab occupancy recovers from 85.9% toward 93-95% by 2029 on the leasing already signed or under LOI, senior housing keeps compounding double-digit same-store NOI for two more years, and the discount rate eases.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25 rather than a bull-tilted default. The bear case is a live operating trend, not a tail: lab occupancy has fallen twelve points in six quarters and same-store lab NOI is still negative. Against that, Q3-2026 lab leasing was the strongest in over a year, guidance was raised, and senior housing same-store NOI grew 25.9%. Neither side has earned extra weight yet.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
